A '''poncelet map''' is an [[Dynamical system#Algebraic dynamical system|algebraic dynamical system]] defined by two [[Conic section|conics]]<ref>{{cite web|title= On Poncelet's Maps|url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.2588|first1=Anna|last1=Cima|first2=Armengol|last2=Gasull|first3=Víctor |last3=Mañosa|date=13 December 2008}}</ref> and the following procedure:
# Pick a starting point on the outer conic
# Draw a line from the point that is tangent to the inner conic
# This line intersects the outer conic at a new point
# Repeat the process from step 2

Given these are algebraic curves and these are relations of intersections and tangents, the map can be defined purely by algebraic equations and therefore is an algebraic dynamical system.<ref>{{citation|title=Poncelet porism and beyond|first1=Vladimir|last1=Dragovic|first2=Milena|last2=Radnovic|author3=Birkhauser}}</ref>

One important property{{Clarify|a theorem cannot be a property of a map...|date=May 2026}} is the [[Poncelet's closure theorem]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Poncelet grid and the billiard in an ellipse|url=https://webdoc.sub.gwdg.de/ebook/serien/e/mpi_mathematik/2006/15.pdf|first1=Mark |last1=Levi |first2=Serge|last2=Tabachnikov}}</ref>
